title: ハビトゥス・場・実践
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
Habitus is a concept used by sociologist Pierre Bourdieu to explain how social history becomes embodied in practical tendencies. Through family life, schooling, work, and other repeated experiences, people develop durable dispositions: ways of noticing, evaluating, moving, speaking, and expecting. These dispositions often operate without an explicit rule being consulted. They are learned, but they may feel natural because their history has been forgotten or was never consciously stated.

Habitus is neither a script that dictates every action nor a collection of freely chosen preferences. Practice arises when dispositions meet a particular field—a structured social setting with positions, expectations, and stakes. A manner of speaking that produces confidence in one field may sound misplaced in another. Resources also matter. Bourdieu used the term capital not only for money but also for socially valued knowledge, credentials, relationships, and recognition. The value of a resource depends on the field in which it is used.

Consider two students entering an unfamiliar seminar. One may already recognize when interruption signals engagement, how disagreement can be softened, and which references carry authority. Another may possess equal intellectual ability yet spend attention decoding these tacit expectations. The example does not prove that family background fixes achievement. It shows one pathway by which institutions can reward familiarity with practices that they treat as neutral.

Because people encounter new fields, reflect on failure, and participate in conflicting settings, dispositions can be adjusted. Change may be slow or uneven, and old tendencies may persist even when conditions change. Habitus therefore helps explain patterned action without reducing people either to rule-following machines or to actors untouched by social history. Its value lies in holding structure and improvisation in the same analysis.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Habitus is an unchangeable list of inherited commands.

options.label: B
options.text: Habitus links socially formed dispositions with action in particular fields without fully determining action.

options.label: C
options.text: Capital means money and nothing else.

options.label: D
options.text: Institutions evaluate only intellectual ability and never familiarity.

questions.answer: The passage links durable, socially formed dispositions to particular fields while preserving adjustment and improvisation. 正解：B。Aは学習と変化を消し、Cはcapitalを金銭だけに限定、Dは制度が慣れを中立な能力として評価する問題と逆です。dispositionは「特定の反応をしやすくする傾向」です。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage not treat habitus as simply a habit or an explicit rule?

options.label: A
options.text: Because habitus consists only of conscious instructions that people consult before acting.

options.label: B
options.text: Because habitus refers to one repeated physical action and excludes evaluation or expectation.

options.label: C
options.text: Because it comprises learned tendencies in perception, evaluation, movement, speech, and expectation that often work without consulting a stated rule.

options.label: D
options.text: Because habitus is biologically inherited and therefore cannot be learned through experience.

questions.answer: Habitus includes a range of practical tendencies learned through repeated social experience, often without conscious rule-following. 正解：C。Aはexplicit ruleとの区別を逆転、Bは範囲を一行動へ縮小、Dはfamily lifeやschoolingによる形成を否定します。embodiedは「振る舞いや感覚として身体化された」です。

questions.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word “tacit” is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: understood in practice without being fully stated

options.label: B
options.text: legally prohibited

options.label: C
options.text: biologically inherited

options.label: D
options.text: measured only in money

questions.answer: Tacit expectations are understood through participation even though they are not fully stated. 正解：A。tacitは「暗黙の・明文化されていない」です。Bの法的禁止、Cの生物学的遺伝、Dの金銭測定とは関係ありません。

questions.prompt: Why can the same manner of speaking signal confidence in one field but seem misplaced in another?

options.label: A
options.text: Because every field assigns the same value to all speaking styles.

options.label: B
options.text: Because speaking styles have fixed value regardless of listeners or stakes.

options.label: C
options.text: Because only the speaker's financial capital determines how an utterance is judged.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the value of a disposition depends on the positions, expectations, and stakes of the field in which it is used.

questions.answer: A manner has no fixed social value outside its setting; the field structures how it is received. 正解：D。A・Bは場による違いを否定し、Cはcapitalを金銭だけに狭めます。fieldは単なる場所ではなく「位置・期待・利害を備えた社会的な場」です。

questions.prompt: Why does the seminar example NOT prove that family background fixes achievement?

options.label: A
options.text: It shows that the two students necessarily receive identical grades.

options.label: B
options.text: It illustrates one possible institutional pathway but does not control other causes, and habitus guides rather than determines outcomes.

options.label: C
options.text: It establishes that intellectual ability never affects seminar participation.

options.label: D
options.text: It proves that dispositions cannot change after people enter a new field.

questions.answer: The example identifies a pathway by which familiarity may be rewarded; it is not a controlled proof of a fixed outcome. 正解：B。A・Cは本文にない必然、Dは最終段落の調整可能性に反します。pathwayは「結果へ影響しうる一つの経路」です。

questions.prompt: What evaluation bias may arise when an institution treats familiarity with its practices as neutral ability?

options.label: A
options.text: Students unfamiliar with the practices will automatically receive extra support.

options.label: B
options.text: Only explicitly stated knowledge will affect assessment.

options.label: C
options.text: People already familiar with tacit interaction styles may be overrated, while equally capable people spend attention decoding those styles.

options.label: D
options.text: All differences in participation will disappear because the institution is neutral.

questions.answer: Familiarity can be mistaken for general ability, disadvantaging people who must first decode unstated expectations. 正解：C。A・Dは偏りが解消すると仮定し、Bは暗黙の期待という問題を消します。neutralはここでは「特定の背景に有利でない普遍的能力のように扱われる」という意味です。

questions.prompt: What two extremes are represented by “rule-following machines” and “actors untouched by social history”?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete structural determination and completely unconstrained individual freedom

options.label: B
options.text: Economic capital and cultural capital

options.label: C
options.text: Conscious learning and biological inheritance

options.label: D
options.text: Slow change and rapid change within the same field

questions.answer: The first extreme makes structure dictate every act; the second ignores social formation altogether. 正解：A。本文は両極端の間に、形成された傾向と状況的なimprovisation（即興的調整）を置きます。B〜Dはこの対比を表していません。

questions.prompt: How can habitus be both durable and changeable according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: It changes instantly whenever a person enters a room and leaves no previous tendency behind.

options.label: B
options.text: It remains permanent because reflection and conflicting settings have no effect.

options.label: C
options.text: It is freely selected anew for every action without influence from earlier experience.

options.label: D
options.text: Past experience makes dispositions persist, while new fields, reflection on failure, and conflicting experiences can adjust them slowly or unevenly.

questions.answer: Durable means persistent, not permanent; new experience can modify dispositions, although old tendencies may remain. 正解：D。Aは変化を即時・完全にし、Bは変化不能、Cは社会史から切り離します。unevenは「一様でなく、領域や人によって異なる」です。

questions.prompt: Which research design best tests whether school participation grades contain tacit expectations?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask one instructor whether the grading system is fair and treat the answer as proof.

options.label: B
options.text: Compare rubrics, coded observations, student interviews, and grades across seminars, then test an explicit rubric before and after without assuming background determines performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Rank students by family background alone and infer their intellectual ability from that ranking.

options.label: D
options.text: Observe only how often students speak, without recording forms of disagreement, instructor reactions, or whether expectations were stated.

questions.answer: The mixed design separates idea quality from familiarity with interaction styles and creates a testable before-and-after comparison. 正解：B。Aは自己申告だけ、Cは背景による決定論、Dは行動の文脈と評価反応を欠きます。rubricは「採点基準表」、code observationsは「一定の基準で観察を分類・記録する」です。
